purpose: Lock system-to-system operation and data authority so every semantic operation, canonical mutation, query, event and domain error has exactly one owning peer while shared infrastructure remains mechanics only.

COMMAND.owner_rule: The semantic owner of the target aggregate/capability is the only peer allowed to accept and commit the mutation.
COMMAND.caller_rule: A caller may request intent but cannot mutate another peer's canonical store, schema, aggregate or transaction directly.
COMMAND.transaction_rule: The receiving owner commits only its local semantic transaction. Cross-peer atomic database transactions are forbidden.
COMMAND.idempotency_rule: Every retriable command crossing a peer boundary must carry an owner-scoped idempotency key or equivalent deterministic deduplication identity.
COMMAND.result_rule: The owner returns a typed accepted/rejected/result envelope; durable state-change facts are emitted as owner events.

QUERY.owner_rule: Authoritative reads are served by the semantic owner or an explicitly owner-authorized projection.
QUERY.side_effect_rule: Queries must not mutate state, acquire leases, publish events that imply mutation, or perform external side effects.
QUERY.store_rule: Callers cannot read another peer's canonical database directly; they query the owner contract or a declared non-authoritative projection.
QUERY.freshness_rule: Projection responses must expose owner version/freshness metadata when stale reads can affect correctness.

API.owner_rule: API transport never transfers semantic ownership. The operation's semantic_owner_system remains authoritative regardless of HTTP, function call, queue, plugin or local transport.
API.routing_rule: Cross-peer APIs must identify operation class, semantic owner, caller, correlation identity and contract version.
API.side_effect_rule: External side-effect execution routes through CONNECTED_ACTIONS when user/provider action authority is required; the originating peer retains its business/domain semantics.
API.bypass_rule: No API may provide a lower-level route that bypasses the semantic owner's command/query authority.

EVENT.owner_rule: Only the semantic owner may emit an authoritative state-change event for its domain. Subscribers cannot gain mutation authority from subscription.
EVENT.fact_rule: Events describe facts already established by the owner; an event cannot be used as a disguised command requiring a subscriber to mutate another owner's domain.
EVENT.identity_rule: Events require stable event identity, originating system, aggregate/entity identity where applicable, owner version/sequence and correlation/causation identity.
EVENT.projection_rule: Caches/read models may update from events but remain non-authoritative and cannot write back into the owner's store.

ERROR.owner_rule: The peer that owns the failed domain operation owns its semantic/domain error code namespace. Shared runtime/transport errors may originate from CORE infrastructure.
ERROR.identity_rule: Cross-peer propagation preserves origin_system, error_code, retryability/category and correlation identity.
ERROR.mapping_rule: Callers may map errors for UX or local orchestration but cannot erase or rebrand the originating semantic error identity.
ERROR.partial_failure_rule: Cross-peer workflows report partial completion explicitly; they must not roll back another peer's already committed transaction by direct database action.

global_operation_rules: Every operation has exactly one semantic_owner_system.
COMMAND and QUERY handlers for owned domain state execute under that semantic owner even when transport/runtime mechanics are provided by CORE.
API is a contract/transport class, not an ownership class.
Authoritative EVENT facts are emitted only by the semantic owner of the fact.
Domain ERROR namespaces belong to the semantic owner; CORE may originate shared runtime/transport/infrastructure errors.
A peer may compose another peer but may not wrap composition as a claim of the provider peer's semantic ownership.
No operation may be registered as mutation-capable under two peer systems.
Historical routing, P6/module-allocation evidence or retired-system records cannot define current operation ownership.

database_contract.canonical_data_rule: Each semantic dataset/aggregate has exactly one peer semantic owner and one mutation authority.
database_contract.physical_storage_rule: CORE may provide generic persistence, transaction, backup/restore, migration-engine and durability mechanics without acquiring semantic ownership of peer data.
database_contract.schema_rule: The semantic peer owns domain schema meaning, invariants and domain migration intent; shared migration execution mechanics may be CORE-provided.
database_contract.write_rule: Direct cross-peer writes are forbidden. No peer may update another peer's canonical tables/documents/aggregates through database credentials or shared repository access.
database_contract.read_rule: Direct cross-peer canonical-store reads are forbidden unless the owner explicitly publishes a read-only projection contract; the projection remains non-authoritative.
database_contract.table_rule: Jointly mutated semantic tables are forbidden. Shared infrastructure tables must not contain ambiguous peer-owned domain fields.
database_contract.transaction_rule: Transaction authority stops at the semantic owner boundary. Cross-peer workflows use commands plus typed results/events; distributed database commit/rollback coupling is forbidden.
database_contract.cache_rule: Caches and projections are derived, non-authoritative, versioned against owner state, invalidated/refreshed from owner contracts/events, and cannot become fallback canonical truth.
database_contract.backup_restore_rule: CORE may own physical backup/restore mechanics; the semantic peer owns restore acceptance invariants and the determination that restored domain state is semantically valid/current.
database_contract.concurrency_rule: Each owner defines domain concurrency/version rules for its aggregates. Callers cannot bypass them with direct writes or out-of-band compare-and-swap.
database_contract.idempotency_rule: Idempotency identity is interpreted and persisted by the command-owning peer; infrastructure may assist storage/dedup but cannot redefine semantic success.

shared_mechanics_consumed: CONNECTED_ACTIONS external retrieval actions where authorized

peer_pair_coverage.rule: The peer_pair_default_policy applies to every ordered pair of distinct systems in peer_systems unless a named seam tightens the contract. A seam may never weaken database/ownership prohibitions.

known_seams.rule: PROGRAMMING commands/queries its semantic operations; CORE may execute shared mechanics but cannot become semantic owner or directly mutate Programming domain state.
BOOK requests artifact mechanics through DOCUMENTS interfaces. DOCUMENTS returns artifacts/results/errors but cannot canonize manuscript or Book state.
PROGRAMMING may request browser/deployment/provider actions but never inherits external side-effect or user-action authority.
CORE may persist Learning bytes/records through shared mechanics but cannot issue Learning semantic mutations or define Learning domain invariants.
CORE performs physical mechanics; BOOK alone decides whether restored Book domain state satisfies Book semantic invariants.
Research evidence may inform Programming but cannot self-canonize Programming state or acquire software-engineering write authority.

existing_contract_compatibility.compatibility_rule: Book routing remains subordinate to this nine-peer blueprint: Book is semantic owner of Book capabilities; RESEARCH_KNOWLEDGE remains owner of bounded research acquisition; only BOOK-COMP-02 has logical canonical Book write authority.

change_control.architecture_change_rule: Any change to active peer set, current capability owner, cross-peer database-write policy or known seam ownership requires an explicit reviewed blueprint update and passing validator.
change_control.capability_change_rule: A capability added/removed/reowned in the current authority-selected crosswalk must fail verification until the blueprint's peer capability projection is reconciled.
change_control.operation_change_rule: A new cross-peer operation must declare interface class and one semantic owner before implementation.
change_control.database_change_rule: A new shared datastore/table may be introduced only as shared mechanics or a read projection with explicit single semantic owner; dual semantic writers are forbidden.
change_control.historical_evidence_rule: Historical interface/routing evidence remains provenance only and cannot silently redefine current ownership.
